questions.stem: What is the atom economy for producing calcium oxide by heating calcium carbonate? CaCO₃ → CaO + CO₂ (Ar: Ca = 40, C = 12, O = 16)
questions.explanation: Atom economy = (Mr of desired product / sum of Mr of all reactants) × 100. Mr of CaO = 56. Mr of CaCO₃ = 100. Atom economy = (56/100) × 100 = 56%. The remaining 44% of the mass ends up as the by-product CO₂.

questions.stem: Which statement correctly describes the difference between atom economy and percentage yield?

options.text: Atom economy measures practical efficiency; percentage yield is theoretical
Atom economy is always higher than percentage yield
Atom economy is calculated from the equation; percentage yield is measured experimentally
Both are measured experimentally in the laboratory

questions.explanation: Atom economy is a theoretical measure calculated directly from the balanced equation — it is fixed for a given reaction. Percentage yield is a practical measure that compares the actual product obtained to the theoretical maximum and varies depending on experimental conditions.
